targetText:
Dialectics tells us that nothing in the world is eternal, everything in the world 
is transient and mutable; nature changes, society changes, habits and customs change, 
conceptions of justice change, truth itself changes : that is why dialectics regards 
everything critically; that is why it denies the existence of a once-and-for-all 
established truth.
summary: Materialist dialectics: nature, human society, and conceptions of truth exist in constant critical motion.
explanation: Dialectics rejects static dogmas and eternal universal truths. Because social reality, productive forces, and legal norms are constantly developing and mutating, philosophy must evaluate all institutions in their concrete historical motion rather than as permanent natural fixtures.

targetText:
It is true that the rural and urban petty bourgeoisie 
now constitute the majority and are really poor, but is that the point? The petty 
bourgeoisie has long constituted the majority, but up to now it has displayed no 
initiative in the struggle for "freedom" without the assistance of the proletariat. 
Why? Because the petty bourgeoisie as a class is not growing; on the contrary, it 
is disintegrating day by day and breaking up into bourgeois and proletarians.
summary: The petty bourgeoisie disintegrates under capitalism while the proletariat steadily expands.
explanation: Refutes the populist argument that socialists should orient toward the petty bourgeoisie merely because of its numerical size. Small producers and shopkeepers are being steadily ruined and proletarianized by capitalist competition. Dialectics aligns with the proletariat because it represents the ascendant, growing class of the future.
